```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
import datetime
import polars as pl
import polarstation
```

`chop(breaks, ...)` bins a column at explicit breakpoints.
This notebook shows how the label text changes across
the four supported dtype families and the three key parameters:
`left_closed`, `extend`, and `fmt`.

All examples use a single break so the output is always two bins.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
def show(df, col_name, expr):
    s = df.ps.with_columns(expr)[col_name]
    cats = s.dtype.categories.to_list()
    return pl.DataFrame({"bin": cats})
```

## Dtype families

### Float (continuous)

Data: `[1.0, 3.0, 7.0, 10.0]`, break at `5.0`.

Float labels treat the break as a mathematical boundary; the interval that
**includes** the break value is the one closed at that end.

| `extend` | `left_closed` | lower bin | upper bin |
|----------|--------------|-----------|-----------|
| `True` (default) | `True` (default) | `[-∞, 5)` | `[5, ∞)` |
| `True` | `False` | `(-∞, 5]` | `(5, ∞]` |
| `False` | `True` | `[1, 5)` | `[5, 10]` |
| `False` | `False` | `[1, 5]` | `(5, 10]` |

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Code

```{python}
df_f = pl.DataFrame({"x": [1.0, 3.0, 7.0, 10.0]})
pl.concat([
    show(df_f, "x", pl.col("x").ps_chop.chop([5.0])).rename({"bin": "ext=T lc=T"}),
    show(df_f, "x", pl.col("x").ps_chop.chop([5.0], left_closed=False)).rename({"bin": "ext=T lc=F"}),
    show(df_f, "x", pl.col("x").ps_chop.chop([5.0], extend=False)).rename({"bin": "ext=F lc=T"}),
    show(df_f, "x", pl.col("x").ps_chop.chop([5.0], extend=False, left_closed=False)).rename({"bin": "ext=F lc=F"}),
], how="horizontal")
```

:::

`extend=True` (default) makes the outermost edges run to ±∞ regardless of
the data range. `extend=False` closes them at the observed min / max.

With `extend=False` and `left_closed=True`, the last interval uses `]` because
its upper bound is finite (the data maximum).

### Integer (discrete)

Data: `[1, 3, 7, 10]` (Int32), break at `5`.

Integer labels convert each half-open cut interval to the equivalent **closed**
discrete range, and use `{x}` for single-element bins.

| `extend` | `left_closed` | lower bin | upper bin |
|----------|--------------|-----------|-----------|
| `True` (default) | `True` (default) | `(-∞, 4]` | `[5, +∞)` |
| `True` | `False` | `(-∞, 5]` | `[6, +∞)` |
| `False` | `True` | `[1, 4]` | `[5, 10]` |
| `False` | `False` | `[1, 5]` | `[6, 10]` |

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Code

```{python}
df_i = pl.DataFrame({"x": pl.Series([1, 3, 7, 10], dtype=pl.Int32)})
pl.concat([
    show(df_i, "x", pl.col("x").ps_chop.chop([5])).rename({"bin": "ext=T lc=T"}),
    show(df_i, "x", pl.col("x").ps_chop.chop([5], left_closed=False)).rename({"bin": "ext=T lc=F"}),
    show(df_i, "x", pl.col("x").ps_chop.chop([5], extend=False)).rename({"bin": "ext=F lc=T"}),
    show(df_i, "x", pl.col("x").ps_chop.chop([5], extend=False, left_closed=False)).rename({"bin": "ext=F lc=F"}),
], how="horizontal")
```

:::

With `left_closed=True` the break value (5) starts the upper bin, so the lower
bin's last integer is 4.  With `left_closed=False` the break belongs to the
lower bin (≤ 5), so the upper bin starts at 6.

### String / Enum (categorical)

Data: `["cat", "dog", "fish", "gull"]`, break at `"dog"`.

`extend` has no effect on categorical columns — the outermost labels always
use the first and last observed category. Breaks are matched against the
sorted category list (or the Enum's defined order).

| `left_closed` | lower bin | upper bin |
|--------------|-----------|-----------|
| `True` (default) | `{cat}` | `[dog, gull]` |
| `False` | `[cat, dog]` | `[fish, gull]` |

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Code

```{python}
df_s = pl.DataFrame({"x": ["cat", "dog", "fish", "gull"]})
pl.concat([
    show(df_s, "x", pl.col("x").ps_chop.chop(["dog"])).rename({"bin": "lc=True"}),
    show(df_s, "x", pl.col("x").ps_chop.chop(["dog"], left_closed=False)).rename({"bin": "lc=False"}),
], how="horizontal")
```

:::

With `left_closed=True` the break ("dog") opens the upper bin, so the lower
bin contains only "cat" → single-element notation `{cat}`.
With `left_closed=False` the break belongs to the lower bin, so lower is
`[cat, dog]` and upper starts at the next category "fish".

Enum columns work identically but the category order comes from the Enum
definition rather than alphabetical sort:

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Code

```{python}
df_e = pl.DataFrame({"x": pl.Series(
    ["low", "medium", "high", "medium"],
    dtype=pl.Enum(["low", "medium", "high"])   # non-alphabetical order
)})
show(df_e, "x", pl.col("x").ps_chop.chop(["medium"]))
```

:::

### Temporal (Date / Datetime / Duration)

Data: four dates spanning 2020, break at `2020-07-01`.

`extend` has no effect on temporal columns — bounds are always the observed
min / max. Labels use `str()` of each value by default.

| `left_closed` | lower bin | upper bin |
|--------------|-----------|-----------|
| `True` (default) | `[2020-01-01, 2020-07-01)` | `[2020-07-01, 2020-12-01]` |
| `False` | `[2020-01-01, 2020-07-01]` | `(2020-07-01, 2020-12-01]` |

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Code

```{python}
D = datetime.date
df_d = pl.DataFrame({"d": [D(2020,1,1), D(2020,4,1), D(2020,9,1), D(2020,12,1)]})
pl.concat([
    show(df_d, "d", pl.col("d").ps_chop.chop([D(2020,7,1)])).rename({"bin": "lc=True"}),
    show(df_d, "d", pl.col("d").ps_chop.chop([D(2020,7,1)], left_closed=False)).rename({"bin": "lc=False"}),
], how="horizontal")
```

:::

## `fmt` — custom label formatting

### Float / Integer: format-spec string or callable

```{python}
df_f = pl.DataFrame({"x": [1.0, 3.0, 7.0, 10.0]})
# Format-spec string
show(df_f, "x", pl.col("x").ps_chop.chop([5.0], fmt=".2f"))
```

```{python}
# Callable
show(df_f, "x", pl.col("x").ps_chop.chop([5.0], fmt=lambda v: f"${v:.0f}"))
```

### String / Enum: callable applied to each category name

```{python}
df_s = pl.DataFrame({"x": ["cat", "dog", "fish", "gull"]})
show(df_s, "x", pl.col("x").ps_chop.chop(["dog"], fmt=str.upper))
```

### Temporal: callable applied to each bound value

```{python}
D = datetime.date
df_d = pl.DataFrame({"d": [D(2020,1,1), D(2020,4,1), D(2020,9,1), D(2020,12,1)]})
show(df_d, "d", pl.col("d").ps_chop.chop([D(2020,7,1)], fmt=lambda d: d.strftime("%b %Y")))
```

## Parameter summary

| Parameter | Float | Integer | String / Enum | Temporal |
|-----------|-------|---------|---------------|----------|
| `left_closed` | controls which side of break is open | same, but label adjusts to show discrete range | controls whether break belongs to lower or upper bin | controls which side is open |
| `extend` | `True` → ±∞ outer labels; `False` → data min/max | same | no effect (always data min/max) | no effect (always data min/max) |
| `fmt` | format-spec string or `Callable[[float], str]` | same | `Callable[[str], str]` | `Callable[[value], str]` |
